articles.title: Autumn is here, and I’ve got five micro-moments of joy to see us through
articles.summary: For those of us who don’t like the chilly seasons, ‘glimmers’ are the way to go. This year mine are woolly, furry, scaly and crunchy. It finally got cold and dark in my neighbourhood last week.
body: It’s time to find some “glimmers”, which is what we’re calling little fragments of cheer now. “Micro moments of happiness that can flip the script on your day” have gone “pretty mainstream”, Grazia magazine said last month, but if you missed the memo, me too. I was busy spiralling into heatwave-fuelled existential dread when trend forecasters explored the glimmer concept this spring – it’s been a low-glimmer time for me.

Grazia’s glimmers included a perfume actually called Glimmer and gel masks that make you look like a ghoul, but for anyone sinking deep into seasonal affective disorder, sheet masks won’t cut it. So I set myself the challenge of suggesting five glimmers I hope are (almost) universally cheering.
First, unearthing pictures of Lenny Kravitz’s massive scarf. The man wears a full flock of sheep round his neck in winter like it’s nothing – how delightful.
Second, who could fail to be thrilled by bluefin tuna returning to UK waters? They can weigh as much as a grand piano – imagine thousands of scaly Steinways hanging out around Whitby!
points: For those of us who don’t like the chilly seasons, ‘glimmers’ are the way to go.
This year mine are woolly, furry, scaly and crunchy.

articles.title: The one change that worked: numb with grief, I sat in the dark, surrounded by strangers – and began to heal
articles.summary: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother. But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity. In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident. His death reset life as I knew it. I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.
body: At home, there were now three of us. We orbited separate corners of the house, each needing a different thing for comfort: for my mum, exercise; for my dad, music; for me, escape.

It was a long, grey January, and I was stuck in the mud. My brain had puffed up like an airbag against the full force of grief; my head was fuzzy and foggy, my thoughts were sludge. I was so sensitive to light and sound that it felt as if a layer of my skin had been peeled off. Mostly, though, I just felt nothing.

I was in limbo. In my early 20s, I couldn’t haunt the house indefinitely. At some point, I would need to rejoin the land of the living. But for now, stepping back on to the hamster wheel felt pointless.

Getting out of the house, at least, I could manage. But where to go? I had seen a sign at my local cinema for an under-25s membership, which offered weekday tickets for £5.99. It would be a relief, I thought, to lose myself in a fantastical world for a few hours. So I pulled on my dad’s coat, made a flask of tea and took a blustery walk down the hill to Greenwich.
points: Life had come crashing to a halt when I lost my brother.
But in the cinema I found comfort and a strange solidarity.
In 2022, my younger brother drowned in an accident.
I had been offered my first proper job; I didn’t take it.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Pumpkin, the rescue cat turned social media star
articles.summary: Struggling to breathe, so big she could barely walk, Pumpkin practically begged for help when we met. Before long I was taking her home. Pumpkin arrived at our animal shelter in March, after her owner passed away.
body: At 25lb (11.3kg), Pumpkin could barely move. Her legs were bowed from the weight and she walked with a waddle. Examining her wasn’t easy. Her breathing became so laboured that she turned blue.
Speaking to her late owner’s daughter, we were able to piece together that Pumpkin was around five and had likely gained weight after two litters and some well-meaning overfeeding.

As a cat dad of three, if I fostered every animal that piqued my interest I would be out of a home. But Pumpkin had these massive, expressive eyes. She doesn’t miaow so everything is communicated through her alien-like gaze. As she lay on her back on the exam table, she was unable to lift her head. Still, she locked eyes with me as if to say: “Help!”

My husband and I decided to bring Pumpkin home to meet our other cats. Jerry is an enormously loud black cat, Doe is sweet and shy, and Dottie is a hunter who gathers my socks in the night. They quickly realised Pumpkin was not threatening. She was far too slow to bother them, couldn’t jump on the counter to eat their food or climb the spiral stairs in our condo. She mostly sleeps on her cat bed, adjusting to her new diet.

articles.title: ‘I’ve become significantly more cautious’: six parents on limiting their kids’ social media and AI use
articles.summary: Quite a few parents aren’t convinced social media and AI are safe, and have been adapting accordingly. When it comes to their kids, many parents don’t trust tech companies any more.
body: Social media companies have spent the better part of the last decade arguing that their platforms are safe for teens, but quite a few parents aren’t convinced. They, along with a growing number of regulators, have increasingly accused companies like Meta of designing products that are addictive to younger users.

AI firm OpenAI, thrust into the public consciousness much more recently than Meta, has had to defend against dozens of lawsuits alleging chatbot ChatGPT lacks safety guardrails. Now, workers at the world’s leading AI firms have warned that their employers prioritize competing with each other over building their models safely.
Both the AI and social media companies have denied the claims, and introduced additional safety measures such as parent-linked teen accounts.
Still, for many parents, lawsuits and public accusations have been enough to change their minds about whether to allow their children to use both social media and AI.
points: Quite a few parents aren’t convinced social media and AI are safe, and have been adapting accordingly.

articles.title: The Shoe and Skirt Combination Sweeping the Street-Style Scene This Month
articles.summary: There was one outfit combination that swept the street style scene this fashion month; pencil skirts and pointed pumps. Here are 7 outfits to try.
body: If there is one key takeaway from this fashion month it’s that 2027 is destined to be the year of the skirt. Miuccia Prada and Raf Simons have asked us all to pause on wearing trousers and dresses for the foreseeable, as the spring/summer 2027 Prada collection featured 63 looks that all centred around a skirt. What Miuccia says always carries weight, and the street style crowd are already responding to her no-trousers directive.

Although the street style galleries feature many different skirt trends, from fall florals to colour-pop midis, if we had to declare one outfit as the uniform of the spring/summer 2027 show circuit it would be a column pencil skirt paired with pointed pumps.

Although you’d be forgiven for thinking there is something rather Apprentice about a suit skirt and court shoes, there is a softness to the styling that stops it being too severe or corporate. Jeanne Damas, for example, wore a pair of black glossy slingbacks with a black tailored skirt, which provided a polished base to her otherwise relaxed weekend staples (she wore a shirt with rolled-up sleeves under a striped jumper and a pair of aviators).
points: There was one outfit combination that swept the street style scene this fashion month; pencil skirts and pointed pumps.

articles.title: The 16 Best Airbnbs in New England Include Cozy Cabins & Coastal Retreats
articles.summary: Planning a trip to the Northeast this season? Stay in one of the best Airbnbs in New England—our list of favorites covers every state (and style).
body: New England is one of those regions packed with charming small towns that shines all year long. In the fall, trade farmstand foraging for apple-picking; meanwhile, mountain hiking trails and coastal shorelines offer a full itinerary for the active traveler in every season. If all you want is your very own quaint cottage, the area has that too—and if you want to experience it firsthand, the best Airbnbs in New England should be your starting point.

New England encompasses Maine, Massachusetts (including the coastal enclaves of Cape Cod and Nantucket ), Vermont, Connecticut, New Hampshire, and Rhode Island; and within each state, you’ll find a lot of vacation rental variety. You can book an airy Swiss-inspired treehouse in one part of the region, only to find an 18th-century cozy cabin a few hours away.
Wherever your Northeast travels take you, get a head start by booking one of these Airbnbs.

This Connecticut cottage lands somewhere between Practical Magic and The Holiday in the best way. The sun-washed interiors are peppered with antique artwork and furnishings, with a bright (and fully updated) lemon yellow kitchen anchoring the space.

articles.title: Schmaltzy Chicken and Stuffing Skillet
articles.summary: The Thanksgiving staple makes for a stellar weeknight dinner.
body: More delicious skillet dinners this way: Chicken Thighs With Spiced Couscous and Carrots; Ruffled Mushroom Pot Pie; and One-Skillet Chicken Pot Pie.

Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Season 2 lb. skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (about 4 medium) on both sides with kosher salt and freshly ground pepper. Pour 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil into a cold large stainless-steel skillet and swirl to coat bottom of pan. Arrange chicken, skin side down, in pan and place over medium-high heat. Cook undisturbed, rotating pan around on burner often to promote even browning, until skin is browned and chicken releases easily from pan, 7–10 minutes. Transfer to a rimmed baking sheet or large plate and arrange skin side up.
points: More delicious skillet dinners this way: Chicken Thighs With Spiced Couscous and Carrots; Ruffled Mushroom Pot Pie; and One-Skillet Chicken Pot Pie.

articles.title: Why is Kim Jones Launching His Eponymous Brand in Hong Kong?
articles.summary: After an illustrious career designing for Louis Vuitton, Dior, and Fendi, Kim Jones is launching his eponymous brand via a standalone store at Hong Kong’s anticipated harborfront development, Central Yards.
body: Widely regarded as one of the most influential forces in modern menswear, Kim Jones is launching his eponymous brand. And he’s doing it in a surprising location: Hong Kong.

“After many years working with incredible houses and collaborators, it feels like the right moment to do something under my own name again. This brings together the things I’ve always been interested in — fashion, art and design — and gives me the space to work with people I admire and explore new ideas. I’m excited about what comes next,” said Jones in a statement. Jones and his longtime right-hand and business partner, Lucy Beeden, will continue to work together on the new label, and both are majority shareholders, the brand confirmed.
Kim Jones’s collaboration with Hiroshi Fujiwara during his Louis Vuitton SS16 menswear show in Paris.

articles.title: What High-Protein, Low-Fuss Recipes Can I Pack for Lunch?
articles.summary: Smashed chickpea sandwiches, green goddess harvest salad, and more hand-picked recipes from our Dear Bon Appétit column.
body: There are millions of recipes on the internet, but you still don’t know what to cook. Tell us about it! Dear Bon Appétit is an advice column where we answer your culinary conundrums with hand-picked recipes and well-seasoned advice. Submit a question here.

I want to be honest with you. After also returning to the office, this was the year that I discovered canned soup. I’ve been telling everyone about it. Like, did you know about canned soup? It’s soup in a can! It stays good for years! You can keep it in your desk and microwave it in the office kitchenette on a moment’s notice. I buy this one from Trader Joe’s in bulk. And they still let me work at this food magazine.

In a previous life, on the weekends, I simmered soup in big pots and froze portions in glass jars, which I labeled and stashed in my deep freezer, then toted to work. Lemony red lentil. Chipotle-cocoa chili. The truth is, I just don’t have it in me lately. So I want to validate you for feeling overwhelmed, like packing lunch while you’re trying to get out the door is too much. Often it is!

articles.title: Vogue’s Fall Travel Capsule Wardrobe Essentials
articles.summary: From walking shoes to lightweight layers, here's everything you need for your fall travel capsule wardrobe.
body: Whether your fall travels are taking you on a cross-country road trip, a far-flung city tour, or a series of weekend getaways, it all starts with assembling the right cast of characters for your vacation wardrobe. That funnel-neck jacket you splurged on in September? It deserves to make its debut on a trip to Paris—but as for the rest of your suitcase, that’s where a little packing savvy comes in.

Luckily, assembling a fall travel capsule wardrobe is easy. You don’t yet have to figure out a Tetris-like storage system for your bulkiest coats. Plus, this is the season of layerable basics; a few sweaters here, a favorite pair of jeans there. You likely already have the majority of pieces available in your closet—and if you don’t, we have suggestions ahead—all that’s left is figuring out what’s actually worth bringing along.

From the packable shoes to the soft knitwear to the practical items you can wear on the plane ride over and reimagine for your itinerary, we put together nine key travel capsule wardrobe essentials worth investing in this autumn.
